lines.text: Is a 225 dollar Optima really better than a 120 dollar battery from Walmart?
He tests 6 batteries and 4 are made by Johnson Controls which also builds the Optima.
And the Duralast costs 40 dollars more than the Walmart Everstart but it looks identical except for the stickers.
The Optima and DieHard are AGM batteries which soak their acid into glass mats so they push out current with less resistance.
beats: ai:cutaway of a car battery showing white fiberglass mats pressed between grey lead plates macro

lines.text: So after one hour on a 10 amp charger the DieHard gains about half a volt which is the most of all six.
Then all six spend 24 hours in a freezer at around zero degrees Fahrenheit.
And the cheap Everstart wins with 766 cold cranking amps while the 225 dollar Optima makes 751.
But at 20 below the two AGMs finish last and the DieHard drops to 580 because cold slows the chemical reaction inside.
beats: ai:frost covered car battery cutaway with lead plates in cold acid

lines.text: Meanwhile the Everstart ties the Duralast at 708 so the cheapest battery in the test wins the cold twice.
And Johnson Controls makes over half the batteries built in America so you are often paying extra for a sticker.
beats: ai:rows of black car batteries moving along a factory conveyor line

lines.text: So which battery is in your car?
